Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
It must also retain callable diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning
the diagnostic interpretation prompt using measured metrics and their definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The supplied code diagnoses item embedding geometry and positive-versus-negative score separation. Model internals are not provided: sequence representations come from `log2feats(sequence)`, and `predict_score(features, items)` produces logits. The probe evaluates every valid sequence position; it does not explicitly extract a final user representation.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` stores the compatibility view, accessing `item_emb`, `log2feats`, `predict_score`, `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`. The latter two are stored but unused.

The loader supplies `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` tensors of shape B × L. Sequences are converted to NumPy before feature extraction. Positive and negative IDs are stacked into B × L × 2 for scoring. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded.

# Probes & Metrics

- **`embedding_collapse_score`**: Samples up to 2,048 nonpadding item embeddings with seed 42, normalizes them, averages off-diagonal pairwise cosine similarities, and maps the result to [0,1]. Higher values indicate greater directional alignment; approximately 0.5 corresponds to mean cosine zero. This is a geometric proxy, not recommendation diversity.
- **`pos_neg_margin_mean` / `pos_neg_margin_p10`**: Mean and lower tenth percentile of positive-minus-negative logits across at most ten training batches. Larger values indicate stronger separation.
- **`pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate`**: Fraction of margins below zero; lower is better.
- **`pos_neg_small_margin_rate`**: Fraction below 0.5; lower indicates fewer weakly separated pairs.
- **`pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown`**: Counts low-margin and wrong-ranking positions and their positive/negative item categories. Categories are unavailable in this task, so category lists should remain empty.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence shuffling, input perturbation, sensitivity testing, or SVD is performed. Margin scoring uses evaluation mode without gradients. The probe does not restore the previous training mode.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` embeds both into a prompt requesting JSON with `status`, `core_findings`, `key_implications`, and `evidence`; it does not itself generate that interpretation.

These probes measure sampled training separation and embedding alignment, not validation HR@10, generalization, calibration, or simulator traits. Margin magnitudes depend on logit scale and sampled negatives. Empty valid-position samples return zero margin statistics, which must not be interpreted as healthy performance.

[RecSys 2025’s sampling-reliability study](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) examines whether sampled evaluations recover full-preference model rankings; earlier [sequential-recommendation experiments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13045) found that both uniform and popularity-based negatives can reverse model ordering. Thus, HR@10 against 99 negatives and full-catalog HR@10 measure different ranking challenges. No located evidence establishes diagnostic probes as reliable predictors of gains across these exact four Amazon datasets.

Practical implication: use scale-invariant probes—positive-item rank percentile, pairwise win rate, and Kendall/Spearman agreement across identical candidate sets—rather than raw score margins. Quantify sampled/full-catalog disagreement using validation-target hit-status disagreement, target-rank percentiles, and model-order reversals across trials. Comparing top-10 lists drawn from different candidate universes directly confounds candidate availability with ranking quality. Keep full-catalog diagnostics supplementary; retain the pinned sampled macro HR@10 for selection. These are proposed diagnostic choices, not experimentally established gains.

For uncertainty, bootstrap paired per-user hit differences within each category, then average the four category means equally; report 95% intervals for category and macro improvements. [Ranking-metric research](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10791-020-09377-x) supports paired user-level comparisons. Such intervals condition on the trained models and fixed candidates; they do not measure training-seed or negative-sampling variability. ## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The supplied code diagnoses item embedding geometry and positive-versus-negative score separation. Model internals are not provided: sequence representations come from `log2feats(sequence)`, and `predict_score(features, items)` produces logits. The probe evaluates every valid sequence position; it does not explicitly extract a final user representation.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` stores the compatibility view, accessing `item_emb`, `log2feats`, `predict_score`, `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`. The latter two are stored but unused.

The loader supplies `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` tensors of shape B × L. Sequences are converted to NumPy before feature extraction. Positive and negative IDs are stacked into B × L × 2 for scoring. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded.

# Probes & Metrics

- **`embedding_collapse_score`**: Samples up to 2,048 nonpadding item embeddings with seed 42, normalizes them, averages off-diagonal pairwise cosine similarities, and maps the result to [0,1]. Higher values indicate greater directional alignment; approximately 0.5 corresponds to mean cosine zero. This is a geometric proxy, not recommendation diversity.
- **`pos_neg_margin_mean` / `pos_neg_margin_p10`**: Mean and lower tenth percentile of positive-minus-negative logits across at most ten training batches. Larger values indicate stronger separation.
- **`pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate`**: Fraction of margins below zero; lower is better.
- **`pos_neg_small_margin_rate`**: Fraction below 0.5; lower indicates fewer weakly separated pairs.
- **`pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown`**: Counts low-margin and wrong-ranking positions and their positive/negative item categories. Categories are unavailable in this task, so category lists should remain empty.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence shuffling, input perturbation, sensitivity testing, or SVD is performed. Margin scoring uses evaluation mode without gradients. The probe does not restore the previous training mode.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` embeds both into a prompt requesting JSON with `status`, `core_findings`, `key_implications`, and `evidence`; it does not itself generate that interpretation.

These probes measure sampled training separation and embedding alignment, not validation HR@10, generalization, calibration, or simulator traits. Margin magnitudes depend on logit scale and sampled negatives. Empty valid-position samples return zero margin statistics, which must not be interpreted as healthy performance.
